source_reviews.disposition: Kashika requires cli-to-cin in bhava/karman before ta. Nyasa explicitly rejects carrying active optionality/prohibition into this passive rule.
The ending following cin is deleted; the printed passive examples agree with the required ta-to-empty transition in every candidate path.
Passive fixes atmanepada endings. The task need not specify a separate pada coordinate.
The general A-final condition supplies yuk before cin. adayi is printed, but Nyasa names dadati/dadhati: the Bhvadi da task is a rule transfer, not a separately printed exact-class paradigm.
Final-vowel vrddhi applies before the relevant nyit suffix; the panel final-vowel forms are rule inferences.
Penultimate a has vrddhi before nyit. Independent example path dad-to-dAd is consistent with cin.
Short penultimate ik permits guna in the stated suffix context; puTa-to-poT and kuka-to-kok illustrate the candidate branch.
Nasal loss requires the stated k/Ng-it environment; bandh retains its nasal in the cin path.
Ric deletion before non-it ardhadhatuka supports intrinsic Curadi class formation; no added causal coordinate is introduced.
Optional mit lengthening is conditional on ni before cin or namul. A separate single-causal Sam control reproduces aSami/aSAmi; it is not part of the ordinary panel.

qualifications: Every task is one aorist/passive/third-person/singular question; eight classes but not a broad release mixture.
Most exact forms are rule-based inferences, not individually printed primary paradigms.
All VP variants are retained, but agreement with the engine is not a proof of complete historical variant coverage.
The additional Ric-Sam optionality control is outside the paid ordinary panel.
Bhvadi da uses the general A-final rule; the printed adayi example should not be represented as exact-class lexical attestation.
Fresh exact inputs do not erase the master split's earlier legacy lexical-family exposure.
